methodological_rigor.justification: Phase 2b randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial with comprehensive biomarker analysis (n=35 randomized, 19 Descartes-08, 16 placebo). Preclinical work in vitro and in vivo well-designed with appropriate controls. Clinical trial methodology follows ICH-GCP with proper IRB oversight. Statistical analysis uses appropriate tests (paired/unpaired t-tests, linear mixed models, FDR correction). Longitudinal sampling design (screen, day 1, months 1, 3, 12) with multiple complementary analytical platforms (flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, TCR sequencing, PhIP-Seq, cytokine profiling).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: RCT in generalized myasthenia gravis with clinical efficacy endpoint (66.7% clinical response, 10/15 Descartes-08 vs placebo). Addresses major unmet need in autoimmune disease treatment. Demonstrates safety and tolerability as outpatient therapy without lymphodepletion. Mechanistic biomarkers (BCMA downregulation, autoreactome retuning, IL-6 reduction) provide evidence for precision immune reset novel to autoimmunity. Potential for broader application to other autoimmune diseases.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for all analytical platforms (flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, TCR-seq, PhIP-Seq, transcriptomics). Pre-planned statistical analyses with FDR correction. Companion clinical outcomes paper referenced. Reporting summary mentioned as available via Nature Portfolio. Methods sufficiently detailed for reproducibility. Data availability statement indicates samples/data from trial available but specific repository/accession details not fully detailed in methods text.

novelty_literature.justification: First placebo-controlled RCT of cell therapy for autoimmunity. Novel mRNA-based CAR-T approach (transient vs integrating vectors) without lymphodepletion distinguishes from CD19 CAR-T approaches. Identifies precision immune reset mechanism via BCMA targeting with preservation of general immunity. First demonstration of autoreactome retuning (PhIP-Seq) in CAR-T autoimmunity context. Links TCR repertoire remodeling to clinical response independently from CAR product.

writing_presentation.justification: Exceptionally clear and well-structured manuscript. Comprehensive methods section with appropriate detail. Results logically organized: preclinical validation → manufacturing characterization → mechanistic biomarkers → functional immunology (TCR, transcriptomics). Figures high quality with excellent legends providing statistical details. Discussion thoroughly contextualizes findings within autoimmune biology and distinguishes from other CAR-T approaches. Limitations acknowledged.

key_strengths: Landmark phase 2b RCT demonstrating proof-of-concept for precision immune reset via BCMA-targeted mRNA CAR-T in myasthenia gravis with 66.7% clinical response rate

Unique combination of transient mRNA-based CAR-T without lymphodepletion, enabling outpatient administration and preserved vaccine titers/immunoglobulins—distinct safety profile from integrating CD19 CAR-T

Comprehensive mechanistic characterization: PhIP-Seq autoreactome retuning, BCMA downregulation on plasmablasts, pDC activation reduction, IL-6 normalization, and TCR repertoire remodeling independent of CAR product

Well-designed preclinical studies (in vitro cytotoxicity, humanized xenografts) followed by rigorous clinical biomarker analysis across multiple platforms (flow cytometry, scRNA-seq, TCR-seq, transcriptomics)

Double-blind, placebo-controlled design isolates drug-specific mechanistic effects; rigorous statistical methods with FDR correction and appropriate test selection (linear mixed effects for cytokines, Dirichlet regression for cell proportions)
key_concerns: Small sample size (n=19 treated, n=16 placebo) limits statistical power for some subgroup analyses; confidence intervals on responder/non-responder comparisons would strengthen claims
Single efficacy measurement timepoint (month 3 primary, month 12 longer-term); lack of dose-response data from phase 2b design limits understanding of optimal dosing/frequency
PhIP-Seq autoreactome changes do not correlate with anti-AChR antibody titers, limiting validation of proposed mechanism; acknowledged as limitation but leaves mechanistic interpretation incomplete
Limited tissue sampling: BCMA+ target cells primarily in bone marrow but sampling limited to circulation; mechanism of on-target effects outside circulation remains inferred

Outpatient setting without lymphodepletion fundamentally different from comparative CD19 CAR-T approaches, making direct clinical efficacy comparison difficult; reliance on historical controls for MG natural history
chief_reviewer.rationale: Outstanding phase 2b RCT establishing new paradigm for autoimmune CAR-T therapy with precision immune reset mechanism and favorable safety profile. Appropriate for Tier 1 journals with emphasis on rigorous biomarker analysis, mechanistic validation, and appropriate statistical methods. Minor revisions would address confidence intervals and mechanistic interpretation of PhIP-Seq findings.
